title: Péterék: Naming a Family or Group

sections.title: -ék: a person and the people around them
sections.content: Add *-ék* to a name or a person word to mean that person together with their family, friends or household: *Kovácsék* is the Kovács family, *Péterék* is Péter and his family (or his group), *a szomszédék* is the neighbour and his family. The ending is always *-ék*, whatever the vowels. A final *-a* or *-e* lengthens first: *Anna* → *Annáék*. The verb is plural, because it is about several people: *Péterék jönnek*.

items.english: The Kovács family lives in Budapest.
On Sunday Péter and his family are coming.
Today we are at Péter's family's place.

sections.content: Case endings go on after *-ék*, exactly as on any noun: *-nál* from this unit gives *Péteréknél*, and *-val/-vel* gives *Péterékkel*. Do not mix up *Péterék* (Péter's group) with *Péterek* (several people called Péter). Later you will add *-hoz/-hez* the same way: *Péterékhez*.
